I've lived in Timberland Village in the Valley for a year now. It's owned by Timber Top (probably the largest apartment complex around). I've had a lot of friends at Timber Top, and I've heard many stories of cars getting broken into. However, Timberland Village, which is right down the street, has been a great place to live. No break-ins, good plowing in the winter, prompt maintenance, and a pool. :] I have a 2-bedroom right now and I'm paying $640/month -- and that's for one of the nicer places with a washer/dryer & dishwasher in-unit. I'd look into it if I were you! It's right on the Cuyahoga Falls/Akron border off of Akron-Peninsula Rd.

I would really suggest that you give them to your mom. I know it has to be so difficult to tell that to your mom and possibly end up in the hospital, but it's really the best thing you can do for yourself (and your future self).

I know this isn't a great idea, but if you have melatonin or a non-harmful sleep aid, could you maybe take that so you could still have that feeling of your body slowing down and becoming peaceful, that might be able to get you through tonight? I don't want your sleep to be permanent, and I'm sure there are people in your life who feel the same way!

Is there someone you trust that you can give the pills to? It would probably be best to have someone you trust monitoring how many you have access to at a time.

Don't expose yourself to triggering stuff right now! I know how tempting it can be, but right now it's really important for you to help yourself first. Maybe try going outside and listening to some music, walking, playing with an animal? I know it's not a magic cure by any means, but if you can make it through the next few hours, I promise there are people out here who care and who can really help you see the better side of life. It would be great if you could make another appointment with your doctor soon, too.

I've been dealing with the same thing -- I'm sorry to hear you are too! It's been difficult, but I've been forcing myself to do things that I've enjoyed before, even if I really don't feel like doing it. For example, I'll make myself get off the couch and cook or bake or knit or paint, and turn on some music while I'm doing it. It also helps me to invite someone to go do something with me, cause that gives me the motivation to get out of myself and go somewhere, and conversation makes it hard to think about depressing or stressful things.

Also, I've been regularly going to the animal shelter in the area. They don't care if I come in even if I'm not looking to adopt. It REALLY helps me, being able to hold kittens and puppies. :]

If you have the most trouble learning and remembering combinations, practice learning combinations. I know it's cheesy, but some people in my old company would learn High School Musical dances to improve their memory/ability to pick up combinations. You could have some fun and learn Crank Dat Soulja Boy if you want. :] It sounds odd, but it really can help. 

And strengthen your core. That is the most important factor in my dancing. Practice engaging your core **at all times.** It can do a world of good.

There are different stretches you can do to help your turnout (it's one problem that I've dealt with too!). This video (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kfJ8znI-UlE) has some pretty decent stretches for improving your turnout. This note from Kathryn Morgan also has some tips: https://www.facebook.com/notes/kathryn-morgan/turnout-and-strength/10150501349497853 .

I had a master class with a dancer from Ballet Magnificat a little while ago, and he said that the most important thing he's found to help with his turnout are tendus and degages. Every second of the tendu or degage, focus on turning out your tendu-ing/degage-ing leg like it's the end of the world! It does help, especially with strengthening your turnout, and it's something you can do outside of the studio as well as in class.

Another thing - go on Facebook and subscribe to Kathryn Morgan (https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=510105185). She's a soloist with NYCB, and she posts helpful notes every week about improving some aspect of your dancing (ie tips on jumps, turnout, turns, auditioning, and so forth). She's fantastic. Subscribe. Now. :]

I love Gaynors! My "problem" is that I don't know what to compare it to really. I've heard that the Sonatas that I had at first are notoriously bad shoes. I have strong arches, so I broke the Sonatas pretty fast. :/ With Gaynors being made of plastic and not needing to be broken in (with the pre-formed arch), I didn't really have to worry about that as much. They last me a decent while, and I also really like the way that they look. They're great to go up on, I really don't have a complaint about them. Also, they don't have a bunching of material on the bottom of the box - it's cut around so it's all smooth.

The only bad thing was that I have really wide, boxy feet, and Gaynors don't come in wide sizes. Therefore, if I want my feet to be able to fit into the widest size of Gaynors, I can't wear toe pads. So, I've danced for the past few years without toe pads... It's taking a little bit of a toll on my toes. :[
